art_instructions: Inside the cozy Greek classroom, show the same low honey-colored desk by a bright window, with the Owl seated upright on the small chair, green scarf visible and her tiny satchel hanging from the chair leg with a few picture cards peeking out. At eye level, the left half of the image is a large chalkboard; write clearly in white chalk across the top line “Α α, Β β, Γ γ,” and on the next line “1 2 3 4 5,” with small headings “γράμματα” above the letters and “ἀριθμοί” above the numbers. The Owl holds a short chalk stick in her right wingtip, finishing the letter Α near the lower corner of the board, while her left wing points down toward five acorns lined in a neat row on the desk to match the numbers. Her round amber eyes are bright and focused, with a small pleased smile to show she is learning. On the desk include a small abacus with green beads, two wooden letter tiles showing “Α” and “Β,” and a stack of simple picture cards. Keep the classroom style consistent: soft blue whitewashed walls with exposed wooden beams, a colorful woven rug under the desk, and warm yellow accents. In the background, place a simple teacher’s podium with a small blue-and-white pottery vase; strong natural light streams from the right-side window, illuminating the board and the Owl. No other characters appear, and all letters and numbers are large enough for children to read clearly.
